html:
Pointe-Noire is the main port and second city of the Republic of the Congo, on the Atlantic coast near old Loango, built from the 1920s as the sea end of the Congo to Ocean railway.

The French chose the deep bay over the old harbour of the Loango kingdom. With the railway finished in 1934 and a deep water port, it became the outlet for timber and minerals of the region, and the capital of the colony of Middle Congo from 1950 to 1958.

From the 1960s it was the base for the offshore oil fields, and it is now the economic capital of the country. Its port also serves landlocked neighbours to the north.
sum: Pointe-Noire is the main port and second city of the Republic of the Congo, on the Atlantic coast near old Loango, built from the 1920s as the sea end of the Congo to Ocean railway.
